label: Fictional sample data
evaluationSummary: Reevaluation 2026-03 (fictional results): DAS-II General Conceptual Ability 98 (average range). Autism eligibility continued based on team review of observation, rating scales and records. CELF-5 Core Language 82; Pragmatics Profile below the criterion for age. Georgia Milestones Grade 4 (spring 2026): ELA Developing Learner; Mathematics Proficient Learner.
strengths: Doc decodes text at grade level, has strong math computation skills, follows a visual schedule independently, and is knowledgeable about maps and transit systems, which motivates him in reading and writing tasks.
needs: Inferential reading comprehension; multi-step math word problems; starting and keeping a conversation going with peers; staying in his assigned area during transitions; asking for a break before frustration builds.
parentConcerns: His family wants him to have more friends at school and to be safer during transitions between rooms and at dismissal.
disabilityImpact: Differences in social communication and difficulty with unplanned changes in routine affect Doc's participation in group instruction, transitions and peer interaction. He needs explicit instruction in pragmatic language and self-regulation, and visual supports.

presentLevels.text: Decodes grade 4 text accurately (98% word accuracy). Answers literal questions 85% and inferential questions 40% on grade 4 passages (3 probes, Aug 2026).
Multi-digit computation 85% accuracy. Two-step word problems 50% accuracy; tends to compute with every number in the problem.
Writes a 3-sentence paragraph with a visual organizer; without one, writes one sentence on topic.
Initiates a conversation with a peer in 1 of 5 structured opportunities; keeps a topic for 1-2 turns. Speech is intelligible; prosody is flat and loud in noisy settings.
ABC data (2 weeks, Aug 2026): leaves his assigned area without permission an average of 6 times a day, mostly during transitions and in noisy settings; returns with one verbal prompt in most cases.
Independent with arrival and unpacking routines. Covers his ears in the cafeteria and gym and uses headphones when offered.

specialFactors.notes: Behavior Intervention Plan attached. Communication: pragmatic language goals and SLP services. Assistive technology: visual schedule, visual timer, break card, noise-reducing headphones (low-tech).

transition.note: Not required: the student is in elementary school (Georgia requires a transition plan by 9th grade entry or age 16).

targetBehaviors.name: Leaving assigned area
targetBehaviors.operationalDefinition: Moving more than 10 feet from his assigned area or group, or out of the room, without adult permission.
targetBehaviors.baseline: Average 6 times a day (10 school days, Aug 2026)

behaviorPlan.settingEvents: Unplanned schedule changes; noisy settings (cafeteria, gym, fire drills).
behaviorPlan.antecedents: Transitions between activities and rooms; loud or crowded settings.
behaviorPlan.consequences: Adult follows and redirects; he is usually returned to the group and the task is delayed.
behaviorPlan.functionStatement: When transitions or noise occur, Doc leaves the area to escape the noisy or unpredictable situation.
replacementBehaviors: Request a break with a break card or words
Use headphones and walk with a peer buddy
behaviorPlan.antecedentStrategies: Visual schedule; 2-minute warnings; headphones offered before noisy events; first/then board; seat away from the door.
behaviorPlan.teachingStrategies: Daily practice of break-card use (RBT, 30 min/day); social narrative about transitions; role-play with peer buddy.
behaviorPlan.reinforcement: Token board; 5 tokens = 5 minutes of map or transit books. Behavior-specific praise for staying with the group.
behaviorPlan.responseStrategies: Calm, minimal verbal redirect to the visual schedule; offer the break card; avoid chasing; staff positioned near exits during transitions.
behaviorPlan.crisisPlan: If he leaves the building, the nearest staff member follows at a safe distance and radios the office; the office contacts the family per school procedure.

dataCollection.method: Daily frequency count and ABC notes
